[MUQATIL:18:103-107/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The greatest losers in deeds are the Christian monks living in cells.
[SIBAWAYH:ولمتقوأنتعملعملالفاعللأنهاليستفىمعنىالفعلالمضارعفإنما#81/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Sībawayh cites الأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَالًا to show a plural adjective with its nūn retained takes an accusative complement, not an iḍāfa or genitive complement.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p209#2/r5] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | Hell is prepared for unbelievers; the next question introduces the people who lose most through their deeds.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī says the people's effort goes astray, though they think they are doing well; Yaḥyā identifies them as the People of the Book.
[AKHFASH:v2p434/r4] AKHFASH, d. 215 · author | holds | الأخسرين أعمالا is accusative because the article and plural ending prevent annexation, leaving أعمالا as an accusative specification.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r1] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | أعمالا is a specification after الأخسرين, clarifying the type of loss.
[NAHHAS:v2p475/r6] NAHHAS, d. 338 · حمزة | prefers | The author judges Hamza’s reading more correct, following Sibawayh’s concern about assimilating lām into nūn, although that assimilation is possible at a distance because the articulation points are close.
[NAHHAS:v2p475/r7] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | ‘The greatest losers in deeds’ uses an accusative of specification.
[SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو بكر الوراق | reports | People ruin their good works by reproaching recipients and demanding thanks, and ruin worship by performing it for show and reputation.
[THALABI:v6p200#2/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · علي بن أبي طالب | reports | He identifies the greatest losers as monks and priests who confined themselves in cloisters.
[THALABI:v6p200#2/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · سعد بن أبي وقاص وابن عباس | reports | They identify them as Jews and Christians, comparing the claim with the description of weary workers entering a blazing fire. | mentions 88:3, 88:4
[THALABI:v6p200#2/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · علي | reports | Asked by Ibn al-Kawwa about the greatest losers, he answers that they are the people of Harura, the Kharijites.
[THALABI:v6p200/r8] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The greatest losers are people who tire themselves in work hoping for profit but end in ruin, like a merchant whose investment fails.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r1] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · علي بن أبي طالب | reports | The worst in deeds are priests and monks.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · سعد بن أبي وقاص | reports | They are Jews and Christians among the People of the Book.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r3] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · علي | reports | Another report identifies them as the people of Harura, the Kharijites.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r4] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | Another interpretation identifies them as followers of religious whims.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r5] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | Another interpretation is people who do good deeds and boast of them.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r6] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | Possible referents are hypocrites whose deeds contradict belief, or people who seek this world and abandon the next.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r7] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | A further possible referent is those who seek this world and abandon the next.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The question asks about people whose deeds make them the greatest losers among creation.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس رواية عطاء | reports | Ibn Abbas identifies them as disbelieving People of the Book.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الكلبي | reports | Al-Kalbi identifies them as Jews and Christians.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · علي | reports | One report from Ali identifies them as monks living in cells.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · علي | reports | Another report from Ali identifies them as the people of Harura, the Kharijites.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r4] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | God asks whether people should be told of those whose deeds are most disastrously lost.
[JISHUMI:v6p4501/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The passage affirms Gog and Magog and the trumpet blast as signs of the Hour.
[JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Those who assume worship of others benefits them are the greatest losers: they exhaust themselves in deeds they think right, then end in the Fire.
[JISHUMI:v6p4503/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · علي | reports | A report says the verse about the greatest losers was revealed concerning monks and priests who confined themselves in monasteries.
[JISHUMI:v6p4503/r4] JISHUMI, d. 494 · سعد بن أبي وقاص، ابن عباس | reports | Another report identifies the greatest losers as Jews and Christians.
[JISHUMI:v6p4503/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو علي | reports | Abu Ali reports that it was revealed concerning the people of Haruraʾ.
[JISHUMI:v6p4503/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الأصم | rejects | Al-Asamm strongly rejects the Haruriyya report because the verse calls them unbelievers in God's signs while they are Muslims.
[JISHUMI:v6p4503/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | prefers | If the report from Ali is authentic, it must be accepted; kufr here can mean rejecting some of God's signs, as rebels do.
[JISHUMI:v6p4506/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The question Will We inform you supports the duty to pursue truth seriously lest one's striving go astray.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The greatest losers exhaust themselves in work expecting reward but end in ruin, like a merchant who buys expecting profit and loses.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص | reports | They identify the losers as Jews and Christians.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | reports | Another view identifies them as monks who confined themselves to monasteries.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · علي بن أبي طالب | reports | He identifies them as the people of Ḥarūrāʾ.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The question about the greatest losers is a taunting rebuke addressed to the disbelievers.
[TABRISI:18:99-105/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The greatest losers in works are disbelieving Jews and Christians whose efforts in worldly life came to nothing while they thought their actions were virtuous acts of obedience and worship.
[TABRISI:18:99-105/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · العياشي | reports | Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits that Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali about the greatest losers: Ali identified scriptural communities who disbelieved and innovated, adding that the Khawarij were not far from them.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | هل is an interrogative particle.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · ابن قتيبة | reports | Ibn Qutayba says هل can carry the same emphatic or rebuking force as the interrogative hamza. | mentions 27:60
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r3] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · أهل التفسير | reports | The first use is a genuine question, illustrated by questions about intercessors, guidance, shared property, and whether Hell is full. | mentions 7:53, 10:35, 30:28, 50:30
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r4] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · أهل التفسير | reports | The second use means قد, as in the questions that introduce accounts of Moses, the disputants, Abraham's guests, the human being, and the Overwhelming Event. | mentions 20:9, 38:21, 51:24, 76:1, 88:1
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r5] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · أهل التفسير | reports | A third use means ما, in rhetorical questions whose implied answer is negative or exclusive. | mentions 2:210, 6:158, 7:53, 16:35, 43:66, 55:60
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r6] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · أهل التفسير | reports | The fourth use means ألا, an inviting or prompting question; the entry applies it to 18:103 and examples about guidance and trade. | mentions 20:10, 26:221, 34:7, 61:10
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · علي والضحاك | reports | One view identifies the worst losers as Christian priests and monks.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · سعد بن أبي وقاص | reports | Another view identifies them as Jews and Christians.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | أعمالا is an accusative specification: الأخسرين alone leaves unclear what was lost, so أعمالا names the kind of loss.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · سعد | reports | In a Bukhari report, Saʿd says the worst losers are Jews and Christians, not the Khawarij: Jews denied Muhammad, and Christians denied Paradise’s food and drink; he called the Khawarij covenant-breakers and wicked.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The question rebukes disbelievers who worship other than God: their efforts and hopes fail, making them the greatest losers in deeds.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r13] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · علي | reports | Ali identifies the worst losers as the Khawarij of Harura; on another occasion he names the monks in their cells, and tells Ibn al-Kawwa that he and his companions are meant.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r14] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عطية | rejects | Ibn Atiyya says these identifications are weakened by the following description of people who disbelieved God’s signs and meeting Him; that fits Meccan idolaters, though Ali and Saʿd named groups that share aspects of the warning.
[QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The verses show that people may work while imagining their deeds good even though their effort is nullified; the cause is corrupt belief or ostentation, and here specifically disbelief.
